newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ business confidence slips in March - NBNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ business confidence slips in March - NBNZ.

text.p: Business confidence slipped in March, with a decline in optimism across all sectors, the National Bank of New Zealand said on Thursday.

The bank's latest survey for its monthly Business Outlook showed a net six percent of respondents anticipated an improvement in general business conditions over the next year, down from 12 percent in February.
NBNZ said the persistently bullish business sector took the biggest fall.

The decline was not evident in respondents' expectations of their own activity outlook, suggesting the fall in confidence was more related to the general state of economic policy than any individual sector concerns.
A net 30 percent of respondents anticipate an increase in their own activity levels, up from 29 percent in February.

Investment intentions remained positive but subdued, mirroring the gradual decline in investment over recent months. A net 13 percent anticipate a rise in investment over the next year, remaining near record low levels.
Interest rate expectations were, on balance, roughly neutral.
"Gone are expectations of continued declines in interest rates, with their current levels expected to persist over the next 12 months," chief economist Adrian Orr said.
The outlook for employment was also weak, with an increased number of respondents expect unemployment to rise. However, employment growth was still expected to be mildly positive.
Pricing intentions remained upward over the next three months, while inflation expectations had stabilised at three percent.
"This certainly smells of an economy at the trough of a business cycle, with the recent easing in monetary conditions a welcome sight."

Orr pointed out that while the Reserve Bank's recent subdued economic projections allowed an easing in monetary policy, Treasurer Winston Peters' upbeat Budget Policy Statement projections supported a rise in government spending.
"Clearly one of them is adrift in their reading of the economic tea leaves, with a clash between monetary and fiscal policy on the horizon," he said.
Only a net 10 percent of respondents expected profits to rise, the same as last month.

"In sum, the outlook remains sluggish. The external sectors remain under pressure, although some light is now a the end of the tunnel. By contrast, the domestic sectors appear to be coming under increasing stress," Orr said.
"It appears that the recent malaise in the export sector is taking its toll on the wider economy."
He said general business confidence remained at a low ebb, and expectations were dissipating for further interest rate falls, renewed export growth and more investment.
